answer: Each firing of the kiln is counted brick by brick, and the kiln book logs the load and the date. A mirror brick fired in another yard fails the count: at the tundra of the clay the colour must match the kiln's own firing, and strange bricks crumble in the frost. Forging a firing means building a kiln, burning it forty times and paying 8,400 in clay and fuel, and the grove mark pressed into every brick is filed in the parish book, so a brick whose firing was never logged is smashed.
